_comment: CFG-1. The complete, authoritative default. Profiles overlay this; a profile is partial and states only what it changes. The orchestrator reads this file at the start of every run and snapshots the merged result into the workspace.
_comment_context: The bounded-context policy. forbid_prior_chapter_prose is no longer a runtime assertion over an assembled prompt: the chapter-writer subagent has its own context window and a tool list of Glob alone, which returns paths and cannot return file contents. The flag stays because it is the thing the architecture is for, and because a future orchestrator that widened the tool list should be failing a stated rule rather than quietly changing one.
_comment_gate: Four critics, aggregated with min, so a chapter is only as good as its worst. length and chatter are arithmetic the orchestrator runs in the shell and they reproduce; continuity and science are subagents and they do not. max_revisions counts rewrites, so 2 allows three drafts.
_comment_style: The style pass may not change a word. The orchestrator compares word counts before and after and discards a pass that moved one, so this tolerance is 0 by intent, not by oversight.
_comment_models: Which model each agent runs on is declared in its own .claude/agents/<name>.md front matter, not here. Putting it in two places is how the two disagree.
_comment_budget: Advisory only on this branch. Nothing enforces these before a call; the orchestrator states the implied call count in its plan and you decide there. The main branch enforces them.
